compiled_state.title: [redistribute-session-commits.sh]: PUBLISH uses 'git checkout -B' -> Destructively resets existing branches incl. session branch
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Incident Overview

Discovered during workflow scenario validation of bug 85f3-8301-c1b0-479d's fix (PR #145, now merged). Line 458 of plugins/dso/scripts/redistribute-session-commits.sh uses 'git checkout -q -B "$_branch" "$MAIN_REF"' to create per-story branches. The '-B' flag CREATES OR RESETS — if a local branch with that name already exists, it gets reset to MAIN_REF, destroying any commits that branch had.

Concretely, if the redistribute tool is run against the d076 epic where one story ID (2abb-11b6-37ca-49dc) happens to match the session branch's name (story/d076-d35e-55db-4843/2abb-11b6-37ca-49dc), running the tool would:
1. Reset the local session branch to origin/main (LOCAL DESTRUCTION)
2. Cherry-pick story commits onto the now-empty branch
3. Attempt push (which would fail without --force)
4. Leave operator with broken local state

## Suggested Fix

1. Detect collision: if any planned branch name matches SESSION_BRANCH (the source range's branch), SKIP that group — its commits already live on the session branch.
2. Replace '-B' with '-b' (create-only, refuses if exists), so the tool fails fast on unexpected name conflicts rather than silently overwriting.
3. Add behavioral tests covering: (a) collision with session branch is skipped with INFO message, (b) collision with pre-existing local branch produces a clear ERROR with no destruction.

## Severity Justification

Priority 1 because the bug could destroy local session-branch state including unpushed commits. Reachable in normal use when the redistribute tool is run against an epic where any story ID matches the session branch name pattern (e.g., any sprint whose Phase F created a story branch and then committed to it directly).

## Related
- Discovered while remediating bug 85f3-8301-c1b0-479d
- Surfaced when planning to apply redistribute to PR #140
